SOURCE: CNBC — retrieved Mon 23 Nov 2026 11:32 GMT
TITLE: 
PUBLISHED: 2026-11-23T05:47:14+0000
Gold rose more than 2% on Monday, rebounding from a more than ​one-year low as a ​rally in the dollar ​took a breather, while market participants looked ahead to upcoming inflation data for further clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate trajectory.Spot gold climbed 2.1% to $3,604.79 ⁠per ‌ounce by 0825 GMT after hitting its lowest ⁠level since September 2025 on Friday. Prices declined 9% last week amid pressure from a hawkish US rate outlook and an AI-linked stocks selloff that prompted some investors to liquidate ‌gold to raise cash.
